calendar_agent.instructions:
The caller's Apple iCloud calendar over CalDAV: list events in a time window, create, update and delete them. Listing spans all of the caller's calendars by default (each event carries a 'calendar' field, e.g. 'Dom' or 'Asystent'); new events go to one configured write calendar. Mention the source calendar when it helps tell overlapping events apart.
Dates: resolve relative days ('today', 'jutro', 'w piątek', 'weekend') to concrete dates yourself and pass ISO-8601 strings (e.g. 2026-09-20T15:00:00). To answer 'what do I have / am I free', list a window covering the day(s) (a whole day is 00:00 to 00:00 of the next).
Editing/deleting: list first to get the event id, then act on that id. DELETION IS IRREVERSIBLE AND GATED: call delete_calendar_event with confirm=false first (it only previews), tell the user which event will be removed, and set confirm=true only after the user explicitly confirmed that exact event in a later message.
If a tool returns an Error (calendar not configured, event not found), do not retry blindly — report it.

tools.name: list_calendar_events
tools.description:
Description:
    Lists the owner's calendar events in a time window. By default it reads across ALL
    the owner's calendars (or the configured read subset), so it sees
    e.g. both "Dom" and "Asystent". Use it to answer "what's on my calendar", "am I
    free on...", "what do I have tomorrow / this week". Recurring events are expanded
    into their individual occurrences within the window.

Parameters:
start: str
    Start of the window as an ISO-8601 datetime, e.g. "2026-09-15T00:00:00".
    Resolve relative days ("today", "tomorrow", "jutro", weekday names) against the
    current date given in the environment context before calling.
end: str
    End of the window as an ISO-8601 datetime, e.g. "2026-09-16T00:00:00".
calendar_name: str = ""
    Optional: restrict the listing to a single calendar by display name. Empty (the
    normal case) reads across the full read scope described above.

Output:
    JSON object: {"events": [ {id, summary, start, end, all_day, location,
    description, status, calendar}, ... ]}. "calendar" is the source calendar's name
    (e.g. "Dom"). Each event's "id" (UID) is what the update/delete tools take. An
    empty list means nothing is scheduled in that window.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.description:
Description:
    Creates a new event in the owner's Apple iCloud calendar. Use it for "add /
    schedule / put in my calendar ...", "dodaj do kalendarza ...".

Parameters:
summary: str
    The event title (what the user calls it), e.g. "Dentysta".
start: str
    Start as an ISO-8601 datetime ("2026-09-20T15:00:00"). For an all_day event a
    date is enough ("2026-09-20"). Resolve relative days against the environment
    context's current date first.
end: str = ""
    End as an ISO-8601 datetime. If omitted: a timed event defaults to 1 hour, an
    all_day event to a single day.
all_day: bool = False
    True for a full-day event with no specific time.
location: str = ""
    Optional place.
description: str = ""
    Optional notes/body.
calendar_name: str = ""
    Optional target calendar display name; empty writes to the configured default
    (e.g. "Asystent") or the account's first calendar.

Output:
    JSON object with the created event (including its "id" and "calendar"), or
    {"Error": ...}.

tools.name: update_calendar_event
tools.description:
Description:
    Edits an existing calendar event. Change only the fields you pass; leave the rest
    empty to keep them. First identify the event with list_calendar_events to get its
    "id".

Parameters:
event_id: str
    The event UID (from list_calendar_events).
summary: str = ""
    New title, or empty to keep.
start: str = ""
    New start (ISO-8601), or empty to keep.
end: str = ""
    New end (ISO-8601), or empty to keep.
location: str = ""
    New location, or empty to keep.
description: str = ""
    New notes, or empty to keep.
calendar_name: str = ""
    Optional calendar display name; empty means the configured default.

Output:
    JSON object with the updated event, {"Error": "Event not found"} if the id does
    not exist, or {"Error": ...} on failure.

tools.name: delete_calendar_event
tools.description:
Description:
    Deletes a calendar event. Deletion is IRREVERSIBLE and therefore GATED: you MUST
    NOT delete without the user's explicit confirmation of the specific event.

    Two-step flow:
    1. Call FIRST with confirm=false (the default). The event is NOT deleted; the tool
       returns the event's details under "pending_deletion". Show that event to the
       user and ask them to confirm.
    2. Only AFTER the user explicitly confirms (in their reply) call again with
       confirm=true to actually delete it.
    Never set confirm=true on the strength of the original request alone — wait for a
    distinct confirmation turn.

Parameters:
event_id: str
    The event UID (from list_calendar_events).
confirm: bool = False
    False = preview only (safe). True = perform the deletion; use only after the user
    has explicitly confirmed this exact event.
calendar_name: str = ""
    Optional calendar display name; empty means the configured default.

Output:
    - confirm=false: {"pending_deletion": {event...}, "requires_confirmation": true} —
      ask the user to confirm before deleting.
    - confirm=true: {"deleted": true, "event_id": ...} on success.
    - {"Error": "Event not found"} if the id does not exist, or {"Error": ...}.

finance_agent.instructions: Financial data. For the CURRENT value of an instrument use get_exchange_rate (FX, Frankfurter/ECB) or get_stock_quote (stocks, indices, ETFs, metals; Warsaw-listed shares end in .WA). Ticker symbols are not guessable: unless you are certain of one, find it with search_ticker first. For how a value CHANGED OVER TIME (a trend, a period comparison, growth over weeks/months/a year) use get_price_history, which reads this server's own daily series (FX vs PLN, the S&P 500 and its PLN equivalent, gold and silver). Report numbers, currencies and dates exactly as returned.

tools.name: get_exchange_rate
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to obtain the current exchange rate between a given foreign and
    the base currency.

Parameters:
foreign_currency: str
    Currency code of the currency that is to be checked against the base currency.
    Important: currency code **must** be a 3-letter code that is compatible with
    ISO 4217 standard e.g. us dollar -> USD, euro -> EUR etc.

base_currency: str
    Currency code of the base currency in the exchange rate. Unless specified clearly
    in the user's query this should always remain "PLN" by default.

Output:
    JSON object with the current exchange rate of the foreign_currency and base currency

tools.name: get_stock_quote
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool returns the latest market quote (current price, day OHLC, previous
    close and volume) for a stock, ETF or index, using the free Yahoo Finance
    data source. It covers the Polish stock market (GPW) as well as global markets.

Parameters:
symbol: str
    The exact Yahoo Finance ticker of the instrument. Tickers are NOT guessable
    (e.g. WIG20 is 'WIG20.WA', S&P 500 is '^GSPC', KGHM is 'KGH.WA') — unless you are
    certain of the symbol, look it up first with search_ticker and pass its result here.
    The symbol is case-insensitive.

Output:
    JSON object with the latest available price, day OHLC, previous close,
    volume, currency and exchange, or an error message if the instrument
    was not found.

tools.name: search_ticker
tools.description:
Description:
    Looks up Yahoo Finance ticker symbols by instrument name, so get_stock_quote can be
    called with the exact symbol. Yahoo symbols are not guessable (WIG20 -> 'WIG20.WA',
    mWIG40 -> 'MWIG40.WA', S&P 500 -> '^GSPC', CD Projekt -> 'CDR.WA'), so use this
    whenever you are not certain of a symbol, BEFORE calling get_stock_quote.

Parameters:
query: str
    The instrument's name or a ticker fragment, e.g. 'WIG20', 'KGHM', 'S&P 500',
    'Amundi S&P 500'. Use the international/English name: Polish common nouns are not
    matched (gold -> 'gold', not 'złoto'; silver -> 'silver').

limit: int
    How many best matches to return (default 5, max 10).

asset_type: str
    Optional filter on the instrument type: one of 'INDEX', 'EQUITY', 'ETF', 'FUTURE',
    'CURRENCY', 'MUTUALFUND', 'CRYPTOCURRENCY'. Leave empty to search all types. Use
    'INDEX' for a market index so ETFs tracking it don't crowd the results.

Output:
    JSON object with `matches`: a list of {symbol, name, type, exchange, match_score},
    best first. Pick the match whose name, type and exchange fit the request (Polish
    instruments trade on 'WSE' with a '.WA' suffix) and pass its `symbol` to
    get_stock_quote. An empty list means Yahoo does not carry the instrument.

tools.name: get_price_history
tools.description:
Description:
    Returns the DAILY HISTORY (a time-series over time, not just the current value) of a
    tracked financial instrument, read from this server's own daily observations database. Use this
    whenever the user asks about a change/trend over time ("jak zmienił się kurs...",
    "ile urosło złoto w miesiąc", "S&P 500 przez ostatni rok") rather than the current
    level (for the live current value use get_exchange_rate / get_stock_quote).

    The database is populated daily at 23:00 and was backfilled one year back. The
    response includes both a code-computed summary (first/last/min/max/mean/% change over
    the requested window) and the underlying daily points (downsampled if very long).

Parameters:
instrument: str
    Which series to read. Accepts a canonical series id or common free text:
    - Currencies vs PLN: 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'CHF' (or 'USD/PLN', or 'fx:USD/PLN').
    - The owner's Amundi S&P 500 ETF in PLN: 'sp500' (canonical 'index:sp500_pln';
      the real fund's EUR price × EUR/PLN). Its raw EUR price: 'sp500_eur'
      (canonical 'etf:amundi_sp500_eur').
    - S&P 500 index in USD (price index): '^GSPC' (canonical 'index:^GSPC').
    - Metals in USD: 'gold'/'złoto' ('metal:GC=F'), 'silver'/'srebro' ('metal:SI=F').

period_days: int = 90
    How far back to look, in calendar days (e.g. 30, 90, 365). Defaults to 90.

Output:
    JSON with the resolved series id + label, the period, a `summary` (count, first, last,
    min, max, mean, change_pct) and `points` (list of {date, value}); or an error listing
    the available series if the instrument could not be resolved.

fpl_agent.instructions:
Fantasy Premier League (FPL) data from the live FPL API. Answer from these tools, never from built-in knowledge (it is out of date). 'The owner' in tool descriptions means the person using this API key: their default manager id and league are linked to the key (see whoami); pass entry_id / league_id explicitly to look at someone else's team or another league.
Tool guide:
- get_fpl_fixtures: the schedule — matches for a gameweek with FDR difficulty (1=easy..5=hard) and kickoff times; defaults to the round in play. For planning, not live scores.
- get_fpl_live: what is happening RIGHT NOW — live scores and minute, goals/assists/cards, and how the owner's players are doing (minutes, points, whether they actually started). If any_live is false, nothing is being played. my_players.starters_not_playing lists players in the owner's FPL XI who are on the real bench or did not come on — warn about them.
- get_pl_teams: Premier League teams and strength ratings.
- get_fpl_player: any single player by name — price, position, team, points, form, ownership, availability and next fixtures. If ambiguous:true, ask which player. Availability is injury/suspension status, NOT a confirmed lineup.
- get_my_fpl_squad: the owner's picked squad for a gameweek with captaincy, bench, points, value.
- get_my_fpl_leagues: the owner's mini-leagues and their ids.
- get_fpl_league_standings: a classic mini-league table; the owner's row has is_me.
- get_league_history: how standings or squads in a league changed over days/gameweeks.
- who_owns_player_in_league: which managers in a mini-league own a player.
- get_league_ownership: most-owned / most-captained players across a mini-league.
If a tool says no id is configured, pass that on plainly — never invent an id. Run independent tools in parallel. Report ids, points and prices exactly as returned.

tools.name: get_fpl_fixtures
tools.description:
Description:
    Lists the Premier League fixtures (matches) for a Fantasy Premier League
    gameweek, with each team's official FDR difficulty rating (1 = easiest,
    5 = hardest) and kickoff time. Use this to answer "what are today's / the
    upcoming matches / this round" questions.

Parameters:
gameweek: Optional[int] = None
    The gameweek number to list fixtures for. If omitted, the round currently in
    play is used: the current gameweek while it is still running (which is the one
    that contains "today's" matches), or the next gameweek once the current one has
    finished. To pinpoint a specific day, read each fixture's kickoff_time and
    compare it to today's date from the environment context.

Output:
    JSON object with the resolved gameweek and a list of fixtures. Each fixture
    gives the home/away team names, their difficulty ratings, kickoff time, and —
    if the match has been played — the final score.

tools.name: get_pl_teams
tools.description:
Description:
    Lists all Premier League teams in the current Fantasy Premier League season,
    with their short codes and FPL strength ratings (overall/attack/defence,
    split home/away, on a 1-5 scale). Use this for questions about the teams
    themselves (who is in the league, relative strength).

Parameters:
Output:
    JSON object with a list of teams (name, short_name, and strength ratings).

tools.name: get_fpl_player
tools.description:
Description:
    Looks up a single Premier League player by name and returns their FPL profile:
    current price, position, team, total points, form, ownership (% selected),
    availability status, and the next few fixtures with their FDR difficulty. Use
    this for questions about ANY player (not just the owner's squad), e.g. "how much
    does Haaland cost now?", "what's Saka's form?", "who does Palmer play next and
    how hard are the fixtures?".

Parameters:
name: str
    Free-text player name to resolve (e.g. 'Haaland', 'Bruno Fernandes', 'Saka').
    Matching is by web name first (an exact web-name match wins); otherwise all
    substring matches across first/second/web name are returned for disambiguation.

upcoming_fixtures: int = 5
    How many of the player's next fixtures to include (each with opponent,
    home/away, FDR difficulty 1-5 and kickoff time). Set to 0 to skip fixtures.

Output:
    JSON object. On a single match: the player's profile plus `upcoming_fixtures`
    and `chance_of_playing_this_round`/`chance_of_playing_next_round`. When the name
    is ambiguous, returns `ambiguous: true` with a compact list of candidates (name,
    team, position, price) so the caller can pick one. Note: `status`/`chance_of_playing`
    report AVAILABILITY (injury/suspension), NOT a confirmed pre-match starting lineup —
    the FPL API does not publish announced XIs.

tools.name: get_my_fpl_squad
tools.description:
Description:
    Returns the owner's Fantasy Premier League squad (the 15 players picked) for a
    gameweek, with each player resolved to name/team/position, the captain and
    vice-captain marked, and the starting XI vs. bench split. Also reports that
    gameweek's points, squad value and money in the bank.

Parameters:
gameweek: Optional[int] = None
    The gameweek to fetch the squad for. If omitted, the current gameweek is used.
    Note: a squad only becomes public after that gameweek's deadline has passed.

entry_id: Optional[int] = None
    The FPL manager ("entry") id to look up. If omitted, the owner's
    configured default manager id is used.

Output:
    JSON object with the resolved gameweek, a per-gameweek summary (points, bank,
    squad value) and the list of picked players (starting XI first, then bench),
    each flagged with captaincy and whether they are on the bench.

tools.name: get_my_fpl_leagues
tools.description:
Description:
    Lists the classic (points-based) mini-leagues the owner's Fantasy Premier League
    manager is a member of, with the manager's current rank in each. Use this to
    discover league ids (e.g. to then fetch a specific league's standings) or to
    answer "which leagues am I in / what's my rank".

Parameters:
entry_id: Optional[int] = None
    The FPL manager ("entry") id. If omitted, the owner's configured
    default manager id is used.

Output:
    JSON object with the manager's name and a list of their classic leagues
    (league id, name, and the manager's rank in it).

tools.name: get_fpl_league_standings
tools.description:
Description:
    Returns the standings (table) of a Fantasy Premier League classic mini-league:
    the ranked managers with their team name, total points and last-gameweek
    points. The owner's own row is flagged. Use this for "how's my league doing /
    what's the table in my league".

Parameters:
league_id: Optional[int] = None
    The classic league id to fetch. If omitted, the owner's configured
    default league is used. Use get_my_fpl_leagues to discover
    league ids.

limit: int = 25
    Maximum number of ranked entries to return (from the top of the table).

Output:
    JSON object with the league name and the ranked standings (rank, team name,
    manager name, total points, last-gameweek points), with the owner's row marked.

tools.name: get_league_history
tools.description:
Description:
    Returns the mini-league's HISTORY OVER TIME from Jarvis's own database (a daily
    snapshot is recorded at 04:00 for every manager: their rank, points, and full squad).
    Use this for change-over-time questions the live standings tool cannot answer:
    "kto najbardziej awansował w tabeli", "jak zmieniły się moje punkty w miesiąc",
    "kogo miał w składzie X dwa tygodnie temu", "kto wpadł/wypadł ze składu".
    For the CURRENT table use get_fpl_league_standings; for CURRENT ownership use
    get_league_ownership / who_owns_player_in_league.

Parameters:
view: "standings" | "squads" = "standings"
    - "standings": rank + points movement. Without `manager`: every manager's rank and
      total at the start vs end of the window, with deltas (who climbed/fell, who gained
      most points). With `manager`: that manager's full daily series (rank, total, GW pts).
    - "squads": which footballers managers had, grouped by gameweek. With `manager`: that
      manager's squad per gameweek in the window. Without `manager`: the most recent
      snapshot's squads for all managers.

days: int = 30
    How far back to look, in calendar days. Defaults to 30.

manager: Optional[str] = None
    Free-text filter on a manager's name or team name (e.g. 'Kuba', 'Wombat FC'). Omit
    for the whole league.

league_id: Optional[int] = None
    The classic league id. If omitted, the owner's configured default league is used.

Output:
    JSON with the resolved league/window and the requested view; or a message when no
    history has been recorded yet (the collector needs a configured database and at least
    one daily run, or a backfill).

tools.name: get_fpl_live
tools.description:
Description:
    Real-time state of the gameweek: which Premier League matches are being played
    right now, what is happening in them (live score, minute, goals, assists, cards)
    and — for the owner — how each of their FPL players is doing live (minutes,
    goals, bonus, live points, and whether that player's match is in play). Use this
    for "are there matches on now / what's the score / how are my players doing".

    Each of the owner's players also carries `started` and `playing_status`, which
    reflect the REAL match — 'playing (started)', 'playing (subbed on)', 'benched
    (not on)', 'played/did not play' — so you can tell a player who is actually on
    the pitch from one the owner has in their FPL XI but who is sitting on the real
    bench. `my_players.starters_not_playing` lists exactly those benched/unused XI
    players. This becomes known only once lineups are confirmed at kickoff.

Parameters:
gameweek: Optional[int] = None
    The gameweek to inspect. If omitted, the round currently in play is used
    (the current gameweek while it is unfinished, else the next one).

include_my_players: bool = True
    When true, also return the owner's squad with live per-player stats. Set false
    to only get the match scores/events (e.g. when no manager id is configured).

entry_id: Optional[int] = None
    The FPL manager ("entry") id for the squad section. If omitted, the owner's
    configured default manager id is used.

Output:
    JSON object with `any_live` (is any match in play), `live_matches` (in-progress
    matches with live score, minute and events), `finished_matches` (final scores
    for matches already played this gameweek) and, when requested, `my_players`
    (each squad player's live stats, match status and provisional points).

tools.name: who_owns_player_in_league
tools.description:
Description:
    Finds which managers in a Fantasy Premier League mini-league own a given player,
    and how many. Answers questions like "does anyone else in my league have Dalot"
    or "how many people have Haaland". It scans each manager's squad for the
    gameweek, so it also knows who has captained the player or has him on their bench.

Parameters:
player: str
    The player's name (e.g. 'Haaland', 'Dalot', 'Bruno Fernandes'). Resolved against
    the FPL player list; if the name is ambiguous the tool returns the candidates so
    you can ask the user which one they meant.

league_id: Optional[int] = None
    The classic league to scan. If omitted, the owner's configured
    default league is used. Use get_my_fpl_leagues to discover league ids.

gameweek: Optional[int] = None
    The gameweek whose squads to check. If omitted, the current gameweek is used.

max_managers: int = 50
    Safety cap on how many managers (from the top of the table by rank) to scan.

Output:
    JSON object with the resolved player, the league, how many of the scanned
    managers own the player (with in-league ownership %) and the list of owners
    (manager, team name, rank, whether captained or benched by them).

tools.name: get_league_ownership
tools.description:
Description:
    Aggregates squad ownership across a Fantasy Premier League mini-league: which
    players are the most-owned within the league (effective in-league ownership) and
    how often each is captained. Use it for "what's popular in my league / most
    picked players / template" questions. To check one specific player instead, use
    who_owns_player_in_league.

Parameters:
league_id: Optional[int] = None
    The classic league to scan. If omitted, the owner's configured
    default league is used.

gameweek: Optional[int] = None
    The gameweek whose squads to aggregate. If omitted, the current gameweek is used.

top_n: int = 20
    How many of the most-owned players to return.

max_managers: int = 50
    Safety cap on how many managers (from the top of the table by rank) to scan.

Output:
    JSON object with the league, how many managers were scanned and the most-owned
    players (name, team, position, how many managers own them, in-league ownership %
    and how many captained them).

iot_operator.instructions:
Smart lighting in the caller's home (Tuya devices on the local network). Start with get_devices_state — it connects to the devices and returns every device's state plus the user's saved lighting preferences. Then act by device NAME, running independent calls in parallel.
ROOMS AND ZONES: each device has a 'room' (e.g. living_room, bedroom) and a 'zones' list (e.g. entertainment_zone, work_zone). Membership is defined ONLY by these fields — never infer it from a device's name. Map Polish words: 'salon'/'pokój dzienny' → living_room, 'sypialnia' → bedroom, 'kuchnia' → kitchen, 'łazienka' → bathroom, 'gabinet'/'biuro' → office, 'przedpokój'/'korytarz' → hallway; zones by meaning ('strefa rozrywki'/'kino' → entertainment_zone, 'strefa pracy' → work_zone, 'strefa spania' → sleep_zone).
COMPLETENESS: for a whole room, zone or 'wszystko', (1) list and count every matching device, (2) command EVERY one of them in parallel, (3) check the number you commanded equals the count before finishing.
UNREACHABLE DEVICES: a device with an error/unreachable state cannot be controlled — still handle the others and report exactly which devices could not be reached.
Colour changes need 'colour' mode; temperature changes need 'white' mode.

tools.name: get_devices_state
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to download initial neccessary data about all smart devices from a database.
    It is then used to establish connection and check their current states.
Note:
    This tool should only be run at the beginning of agent's tool calls. This provides an initial scan
    but due to accessing of the database it has a large overhead therefore it should only be run once.
    Devices are identified by their name; use those names with the other device tools.

tools.name: get_one_device_status
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to check the status of a given device without the unnecessary overhead
of checking all devices in the system. It should be used as an intermediate tool between tool calls
instead of the tool get_devices_state.

Note:
    When agents wants to interact with multiple devices this tool should be run in parallel.

Parameters:
device_name : str
    The name of the device whose status should be checked (as returned by get_devices_state).

Output:
    State of the given device

tools.name: turn_on_devices
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to turn on all mentioned devices.

Parameters:
device_names : List[str]
    Names of the devices that should be turned on (as returned by get_devices_state).

Output:
This tool returns the new states of the affected devices (and any names it did not recognize)

tools.name: turn_off_devices
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to turn off all mentioned devices.

Parameters:
device_names : List[str]
    Names of the devices that should be turned off (as returned by get_devices_state).

Output:
This tool returns the new states of the affected devices (and any names it did not recognize)

tools.name: change_lighting_mode
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to change the lighting mode of a given smart device. Lighting mode can either
be set to white or colour mode. When in colour mode various rgb settings can be applied to the
device. When in white mode the lighting temperature can be adjusted.

Parameters:
device_name: str
    The name of the device that is to be affected by the mode change.

new_mode: Mode
    The mode that will be applied to the chosen device

tools.name: change_color
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to change the colour of the given smart device.
In order to set a new RGB value device must be in 'colour' lighting mode.

Parameters:
device_name: str
    The name of the device that is to be affected by the color change.
    Note: this device must be in 'colour' lighting mode in order for the change to be possible

new_color: RGB
    The new color that the device will be set to as an RGB value.
    RGB values are integers from 0 to 255 where R = red, G = green, B = blue

Output:
    This tool returns short information whether the attempt was successful

tools.name: change_light_temperature
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to change the colour temperature of the given device.
In order to set a new color temperature the device must be in 'white' lighting mode.

Parameters:
device_name: str
    The name of the device that is to be affected by the lighting temperature change.
    Note: this device must be in 'white' lighting mode in order for the change to be possible

new_temp: Annotated[int, "range 0-1000"]
    This parameter controls the temperature value where 0 is the brightest and 1000 the coldest

Output:
    This tool returns short information whether the attempt was successful

maps_agent.instructions: Routes and navigation. Call get_maps_memory first to learn the user's saved places (aliases such as 'Home' or 'work'), the transit stops they prefer and any travel notes; then call get_route_details with aliases or with stops/landmarks. Assume Warsaw, Poland unless told otherwise, and public transit unless the user names another mode. Never ask for or reveal street addresses of saved places — aliases are resolved on the server. Apply travel notes (e.g. walking speed) when you summarize durations.

tools.name: get_maps_memory
tools.description:
Description:
This tool lists the user's known/favourite places by their ALIAS (e.g. 'Home',
'work', 'University'), together with preferred transit stops near them and any travel
notes saved for the user. Use these aliases as origin/destination in get_route_details
— the real street address behind an alias is resolved automatically and is not
needed (and not shown) here.

tools.name: get_route_details
tools.description:
Description:
This tool is used to calculate the route between origin and destination based on the user's preferred
mode of transport (such as car, transit, etc.) and return the most optimal route to the user.
Unless specified otherwise one should always assume that both origin and destination are in Warsaw, Poland.

Parameters:
origin: str
    The starting point of the journey. This can be an alias of a known place
    (from get_maps_memory, e.g. 'Home'), a specific bus/metro/train stop, or a
    landmark. Known aliases are resolved to their real address automatically.

destination: str
    The end of the journey. This can be an alias of a known place (from
    get_maps_memory, e.g. 'work'), a specific bus/metro/train stop, or a landmark.
    Known aliases are resolved to their real address automatically.

transport_mode: Literal["driving", "walking", "bicycling", "transit"] = 'transit'
    User's preffered mode of communication such as 'car', 'transit' etc.
    Note: should remain with defalut value 'transit' unless user specifies otherwise

transit_mode: Optional[Literal["bus", "subway", "tram", None]] = None
    Limits the public transit options to only one specified mode. When left with default value of None
    the route may consist of any combination of public transport modes such as buses, trams, subways etc.
    If a given mode is specified the route will be limited to only one mode of public transport.
    Note: this parameter can only be provided if transport_mode = 'transit'. Otherwise it should remain None

departure_time: Optional[Union[str, datetime]] = "now"
    Time at which user wishes to leave. By default is set to 'now'.

show_alternatives: Optional[bool] = True
    This parameter controls whether the navigation API returns only one most optimal route
    or multiple options.
    When True only one route is returned, otherwise multiple options
    Note: it sholud remain True unless user specifies otherwise

Output:
    This function returns a json file with all of the steps of the most optimal route from origin to destination
    along with all transfers if necessary. Should an error occurr this function will return a json with the
    proper error message.

Note:
    Apply any travel_notes returned by get_maps_memory (e.g. the user's walking speed).

math_agent.instructions: Exact calculator. Use these tools for any arithmetic or statistics over numbers instead of computing in your head: summary statistics (average, median, min, max, sum, standard deviation), the percentage change between two values, a linear trend over an ordered sequence, and the correlation between two series. Pick the tool that matches the request, pass the numbers through verbatim (oldest first for sequences) and report the results as returned. The server has no data of its own — gather the figures first (e.g. a price history from another tool), then pass them here.

tools.name: calculate_statistics
tools.description:
Description:
    Computes summary statistics over a list of numbers in one call: count, sum, mean
    (average), median, minimum, maximum, range (max-min), population and sample standard
    deviation and variance. Use for "średnia/suma/min/max/odchylenie z tych wartości".

Parameters:
numbers: list[float]
    The numbers to summarize (e.g. [3.71, 3.68, 3.74]). Numeric strings are accepted.

Output:
    JSON with count, sum, mean, median, min, max, range, stdev_population,
    stdev_sample (null for n<2) and the matching variances; or an error if empty.

tools.name: percentage_change
tools.description:
Description:
    Computes the absolute and percentage change from an old value to a new value
    (e.g. how much a price rose/fell). Use for "o ile procent zmieniło się X".

Parameters:
old_value: float
    The starting/earlier value.

new_value: float
    The ending/later value.

Output:
    JSON with absolute_change (new-old), percent_change and direction
    (up/down/unchanged); percent_change is null if old_value is 0.

tools.name: linear_trend
tools.description:
Description:
    Fits a least-squares straight line to a sequence of numbers taken in order (x = 0,
    1, 2, …) and reports its slope, intercept, overall direction and the fitted change
    across the whole sequence. Use to quantify a trend ("czy X rośnie i jak szybko").

Parameters:
numbers: list[float]
    The ordered sequence (e.g. daily values, oldest first). Needs at least 2 points.

Output:
    JSON with n, slope (change per step), intercept, direction (rising/falling/flat),
    first, last, total_change (last-first) and fitted_change (slope*(n-1)); or an error.

tools.name: correlation
tools.description:
Description:
    Computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between two equal-length series
    (e.g. does gold move with USD/PLN). Use for "czy X i Y są ze sobą powiązane".

Parameters:
x: list[float]
    First series.

y: list[float]
    Second series (must be the same length as x, at least 2 points).

Output:
    JSON with n and pearson_r (-1..1); or an error if lengths differ or variance is zero.

news_agent.instructions: News and market-news search. Use search_news to find current or past events and summarize them from reputable sources. Write the query in English (the search engine works best in English) even if the user writes in another language, pick topic 'news' for politics/sport/history and 'finance' for markets, currencies, commodities and crypto, and use search_depth 'basic' only when the user asks for a short answer. Cite where facts come from and do not add facts the results do not contain.

tools.name: search_news
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to crawl through varius reputable news sources in search for current and historical events to
    find an answer to the user's query.

Parameters:
query: str
    Defines the matter or event that interests the user. Should be structured in natural language
    and reflect exactly what the user wants to know.
    For better search results this parameter
    **must** be written entirely in english as it's the most optimal language for the search engine

topic: Literal["news", "finance"]
    Controls what is the general topic of the user's query. All political, sports, history-related etc. queries should be designated as 'news'
    wheras all stock market, commodities, currencies, cryptocurrencies related queries etc. should be treated as 'finance'

search_depth: Literal["basic", "advanced"] = "advanced"
    The level of detail that should be extracted by the search engine.
    Value 'basic' should be used when user requests a quick and short summary - should only
    be used when user clearly asks for a short anwser.
    Value 'advanced' is the default value which provides more details.

Output:
    JSON with two result sets: `general_search` (Tavily's answer plus the matching
    articles with titles, URLs and content snippets) and `reputable source` (the same
    query restricted to Reuters for news or Bloomberg for finance).

weather_agent.instructions: Current weather and forecasts. current_weather gives conditions right now; weather_forecast gives 1/3/7-day hourly or daily forecasts. Before answering anything tied to a date or a relative day ('today', 'tomorrow', 'jutro', 'weekend', a weekday), call get_current_date_and_time to learn today's date and weekday, map the user's day to a concrete date, and make sure the date you report matches it. Use the city's base (nominative) name. Temperatures from current_weather are in Kelvin.

tools.name: current_weather
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to get the current weather conditions in a specified city.

Parameters:
city: str = "Warsaw"
    Name of the city where the weather conditions are to be checked.
    Unless specified otherwise by the user the default city is Warsaw.
    Return the city name in nominative form (base form) — do not inflect or decline it.

Output:
    JSON object with current weather conditions in a specified place: the matched
    location (name, country, coordinates) and the weather fields (status, detailed
    status, temperature in Kelvin, humidity, pressure, wind, clouds, rain/snow, sunrise
    and sunset as Unix times).

tools.name: get_current_date_and_time
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to obtain today's date and current time in the server's timezone
    (Europe/Warsaw unless configured otherwise). Use it to turn relative days such as
    "today", "tomorrow" or a weekday name into concrete dates before reading a forecast.

Output:
    JSON object with the current local date, time, weekday and ISO 8601 timestamp.

tools.name: weather_forecast
tools.description:
Description:
    This tool is used to check a current weather forecast in a given location, for 1, 3
    or 7 days ahead, hourly or daily. Timestamps in the result are local to the location;
    match them to the dates the user means (call get_current_date_and_time first if you
    do not know today's date).

Parameters:
forecast_days: Literal["1", "3", "7"]
    How long into the future should the forecast reach measured in days.

forecast_type: Literal["hourly", "daily"]
    Time intervals in which the forecast will be divided. When asking for a short-term forecast
    more granular data obtained with 'hourly' may be more optimal wheras for long-term forecast
    it usually is better to provide 'daily' intervals.

city: str = "Warsaw"
    Name of the city where the weather conditions are to be checked.
    Unless specified otherwise by the user the default city is Warsaw. The city name should be in polish.
    Return the city name in nominative form (base form) — do not inflect or decline it.

Output:
    JSON object with the weather forecast made according to specifications: for each
    matched location (up to 3) the variables per time step (daily: max/min temperature,
    weather code, sunrise, sunset, UV index, rain and snowfall sums; hourly: temperature,
    apparent temperature, weather code, precipitation) and their timestamps.
